selectedRuntime.licensingConclusion: Reviewed linked components use Apache, MIT, BSD, ISC, zlib/libpng or IJG permissive terms. Preserve full copyright, licence and IJG acknowledgement texts. openlibm LGPL test-program notices are retained, but those test programs are not built by install-static. Project restrictions cannot override third-party rights.

security.assessment: Core includes older codecs: libpng 1.6.38.git, libwebp 1.2.2, libtiff 4.3.0, giflib 5.1.4, IJG jpeg 9a, Leptonica 1.83.0 and zlib 1.2.12. Native review found libpng advisories and CVE-2023-4863 affecting older WebP versions; npm audit cannot clear these compiled libraries. The editor now serializes its bounded opaque canvas as fixed P6 RGB (20 million pixels maximum), not PNG. User-provided image headers, ancillary chunks, compression streams, native PDF files and URLs never enter this OCR path. Pinned language models are raw, not gzip. This avoids those compressed-image decoder entry paths in the editor but does not remove the old codecs from the binary, assess all PNM/Tesseract/model code, or certify exact-binary safety. A refreshed minimal native graph or independent exact-binary clearance remains a public-release blocker.
security.controlledInput: local-ocr-pixels.ts emits a fixed P6 header, exact bounded RGB byte count and explicit white alpha composition. The worker independently validates canonical P6 and refuses shared/truncated/alternate-format data before spawning and after asynchronous initialization, immediately before cloning into recognition.
security.researchCandidate: ocr-minimal-candidate.json records a separate baseline source build with Leptonica 1.87.0 and no optional compressed-image codec archives. The revised research bindings use public Leptonica getters instead of internal layouts; 25 raw/ownership calls trap, and 100 owned allocation/read/free cycles plus English/French synthetic worker smoke passed. Exact artifact and repeat-build evidence are recorded separately. Existing app assets are unchanged; old Tesseract/warnings, the wider API, full licensing/security, variant, export and reference-platform reviews remain gates. This research does not set completeNativeVulnerabilityClearance.
security.pixelMetadataIsolation: A fixed 512-space ASCII prefix keeps all RGB pixels outside the unchanged tesseract.js 7.0.0 setImage helper's first-500-byte EXIF-pattern scan. Raster pixels remain unchanged. Canonical prefix, depth, dimensions, exact body size and non-shared ownership are checked before worker creation and again after initialization. Header mutation cases and a forged-EXIF pixel pattern are tested; this is bounded parser exposure reduction, not whole-native fuzz clearance.

notes: The native inventory above is partial, not an SBOM or a distribution approval.
Base images are digest-pinned, but Debian apt dependencies are not individually pinned. Do not infer future rebuilt image identity from this test.
The worker currently performs OCR on page renders then overlays a text-only PDF onto the source; visible scan preservation has one synthetic-case verification, not broad PDF/scan coverage.
The local editor now uses the separate browser WASM path. This native container is not adopted for editor OCR and remains blocked for public distribution.
Pinned dependencies are adopted for local development after artifact/source and linked-notice review. Complete final-distribution SBOM and native security clearance remain release work.

The core maintainer identifies permissive compiled third-party libraries and asks that required attributions be included. An open issue is not proof that every current npm artifact lacks notices; the exact artifact still requires inspection.

Implemented local-only route uses existing PDF.js rendering and PDF composition. Tests cover unchanged scan pixels, source immutability, actual-output review, undo/redo, independent extraction and immediate worker cleanup.
All worker/core/model paths must be local or self-hosted; default CDN downloads are not an approved configuration. Scans must remain visually unchanged.
